# Silver Reed: stallholder pack

Collection: basketry.

## Packing down

- Begin packing down after the public market closes at 16:00.
- Count the remaining baskets against the opening list before putting them into their transport box.
- Return the trays label cards to the pouch used on the way to the market.
- Wrap the bowls separately from the display stands so the labels remain readable.
- Take all your unsold stock and packaging away; none is left for the venue to dispose of.
- Check beneath the table for the box that carried the hampers and platters.
- Put the stands and boxes sample cards in the notebook rather than with the wrapping scraps.
- Keep the return count of screens beside the sales record until you have checked it at home.
- Put the last sculptures label on top of its bundle so it is easy to find on arrival home.

## Notes after the market

- Compare the remaining baskets count with the entries in your sales notebook.
- Keep the customer questions about trays with the photographs of that collection.
- Write down whether another display stand would help show the bowls.
- Check whether the price cards for hampers can be reused at the next market.
- Record any colour requests for platters without treating them as confirmed orders.
- Put the sample card for stands back in the display kit once you have finished the stock count.
- Keep the final packing list for boxes with the matching box.
- Note which wrapping sizes were used for screens so the supplies can be replenished.
- File the sculptures receipt copies with the rest of this market's paperwork.

## Stock for this visit

- Bring 16 baskets from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 17 trays from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 18 bowls from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 19 hampers from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 20 platters from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 21 stands from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 22 boxes from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 23 screens from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.
- Bring 24 sculptures from the Silver Reed basketry collection, with their matching stock labels.

## Packing the collection

- Put the baskets in the first box, with a handwritten count on a card inside the lid.
- Wrap the trays separately so their labels are not hidden by the protective paper.
- Leave one example of the bowls near the top for setting up the front of the display.
- Bring your own table covering; the venue provides a bare table.
- Keep the price cards for hampers with that group rather than in the general stationery bag.
- The platters go in the shallow box that can slide beneath the table during the market.
- Use the older packing sleeves for stands; their creases will be hidden underneath the display.
- Check that the small labels for boxes have not stuck to the packing paper.
- Put the screens and sculptures in separate bundles to simplify the opening stock count.

## Arrival and access

- The name on your stall envelope is Silver Reed; keep the envelope with the collection until unpacking.
- Bring delivery vehicles to the Mill Lane gate for unloading; the High Street front steps are pedestrian access.
- Carry the lightweight baskets box separately from the heavier display materials.
- Place the box of trays beside your own table while you unpack, within its marked space.
- Stallholder entry for setting up starts at 08:00; do not begin setting up before that time.
- Keep the label sheet for bowls to hand instead of leaving it in the vehicle.
- Put the empty transport bags beneath your own table once the hampers are unpacked.
- Check the stall name against your envelope before laying out the stock.
- Do not leave a delivery vehicle blocking the unloading gate after the boxes are out.

## Building the display

- Place the baskets on the left, with one label visible from the front of the table.
- Put the tallest trays behind the smaller pieces so they do not hide the price cards.
- Leave a clear patch beside the bowls for showing a customer the details of one piece.
- Keep every display and spare box inside the marked stall space so the aisle remains clear.
- Group the hampers by finish, keeping the spare examples below their display group.
- Put the platters near the sample card that explains how that part of the collection was made.
- Lay out only a few stands at once and bring replacements from the stock box as they sell.
- The boxes and screens use the two small stands from your own display kit.
- Keep the sculptures label facing outward even when there is only one example left.

## Explaining the work

- The collection description calls these pieces basketry, using the wording on your own labels.
- Show the back of a sample baskets when a customer asks about its finish.
- Keep the sample for trays separate from the pieces counted as available stock.
- Explain that the bowls in this batch share a design, while small surface details vary.
- Use the photograph card to show the earlier stages of making the hampers.
- Let the maker card answer questions about where the platters were made.
- The sketch beside the stands shows an alternative colour rather than another item for sale.
- Use the same collection names for boxes on the display and on the receipt.
- Keep a sample label for screens and sculptures in your notebook after the market.

## Prices and payments

- The price cards for baskets belong beside that group, with the stock code facing you.
- Keep the replacement labels for trays in the stationery pouch rather than under the display.
- You supply and manage your own payment method; the free guest wireless network is available.
- Check the description on the receipt when a customer buys one of the bowls.
- Write the code for the hampers in the sales notebook before wrapping the purchase.
- When two platters are sold together, record each stock code on its own entry.
- The sample stands stays marked as a sample so it is not included in the sold total.
- Keep a pencil beside the boxes stock card for updating the remaining quantity.
- Check that descriptions for screens and sculptures are readable on the receipt copy.

## Keeping track of stock

- Count the baskets left in the box before putting replacements out on the table.
- Cross through the stock code when a displayed example of trays is sold.
- The spare labels for bowls use the same collection name as the display card.
- Keep the hampers packing sleeves in their own box so their remaining count is easy to check.
- Make a note if a customer asks about another colour of platters.
- Put a mark beside the stands code when that design has only its display sample left.
- The stock card for boxes stays with the notebook even if that group sells out.
- Check the count of screens before starting to pack them for the return journey.
- Keep the final count for sculptures on the original stock card rather than on loose paper.

## Breaks and refreshments

- The cafe sells its own food and drinks separately from the goods on your stall.
- Leave the baskets price card visible if you cover the stall while taking a break.
- Put the notebook beside the trays stock box so your companion can find it.
- Take used cafe mugs back to the cafe counter; do not leave them at the market exit.
- Keep cups off the display area beside the bowls and use your own small side tray instead.
- Leave the wrapping supplies for hampers within reach of the person looking after the stall.
- Tell your companion which platters are samples before handing the stall over.
- Keep the stands and boxes stock codes on the same page while the companion is helping.
- Use the notebook for questions about screens and sculptures that need your answer later.

## Wrapping purchases

- Bring your own bags and wrapping; the venue does not supply packaging for purchases.
- Use a small piece of your packing paper between two baskets bought together.
- Keep the labels with the trays when a customer wants them wrapped separately.
- Use the larger bag for the bowls instead of folding their information card.
- Check the receipt against the number of hampers before sealing the bag.
- Put the maker card beside the platters so it can be read without unwrapping everything.
- The reused sleeves for stands are for transporting stock, not the customer display.
- Leave the labels readable when wrapping the boxes and screens together.
- The smallest sculptures fit in the shallow paper packets in your wrapping box.

## During public opening

- The public market runs from 10:00 until 16:00; keep the collection available during those hours.
- Use a single example of the baskets to explain the collection rather than unpacking every spare.
- Keep the information card beside the trays even when the display is rearranged.
- Put any customer questions about the bowls on the page with their stock codes.
- Replace the hampers price card if its writing becomes hard to read during the day.
- The spare platters are in the same box used for transport and need not all be displayed.
- Keep the stands sample with its descriptive card while showing it to a customer.
- When a group of boxes sells out, remove that price card rather than leaving an empty group.
- Leave the last screens and sculptures near their respective stock labels.
